customer_message: How long do I have to dispute a charge?

output.reply:
You have **60 days** from the transaction date to dispute a charge. The dispute must be filed within that window. If the charge is older than 60 days, you'll need to call Tidewell Bank support at 1-800-555-0199 (Monday to Friday, 8am to 8pm) to ask about it.

(Source: Disputing a transaction)

Source: Disputing a transaction > When you can dispute a charge
You can dispute a posted charge on your Tidewell Bank account if you didn't make it, didn't receive what you paid for, were charged twice, or were charged the wrong amount. Disputes must be filed within 60 days of the transaction date.

Source: Disputing a transaction > Charges older than 60 days
Charges older than 60 days can't be disputed through chat. To ask about an older charge, call Tidewell Bank support at 1-800-555-0199, Monday to Friday, 8am to 8pm.

Source: Pending and posted transactions > Disputing a pending transaction
Pending transactions can't be disputed until they post. If a charge still looks wrong after it posts, you can dispute it within 60 days of the transaction date.

Source: Disputing a transaction > What happens after you file a dispute
When you file a dispute, you receive a case number starting with DSP. A specialist reviews every dispute and contacts you within 10 business days. Each charge can only be disputed once; if a dispute already exists for a charge, we'll share its case number and status.

Source: Disputing a transaction > Pending charges
Pending charges can't be disputed until they post, which usually takes a few business days. Many charges that look wrong while pending, such as hotel or gas station holds, are corrected automatically when they post.

A frozen card can't be used for new purchases. Your accounts stay open, and the money in them is not affected. Freezing a card does not cancel or replace it.

If your Tidewell Bank card is lost, stolen, or has been used without your permission, you can freeze it in chat after verifying your identity. Freezing a card takes effect immediately, and new purchases on the card are declined.

customer_message: Do your savings accounts come with a debit card?

output.reply: No, Tidewell Bank savings accounts don't come with a debit card. They're designed for setting money aside and earning interest. If you need a debit card for everyday spending, a checking account would be a better fit—those come with one. (Source: Account types > Savings accounts)
